newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end with pared losses.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end with pared losses.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were broadly lower on producer selling and light fund liquidation but a late industry buying helped values to end off the day's lows.
Traders said a wave of origin hedge selling and fund sell-stops earlier hammered prices from the opening bell.
"But there was some reasonable support underneath from the industry buying," said one trader.
By the close, most-active November stood $17 off at $1,488 a tonne after touching the day's low of $1,475 and just above key technical support at $1,471.
Other positions were $6 to $20 down. Total volume reached 3,561 lots.
Traders said the sell-off came after news major growers decided, as expected, to maintain their existing export programme following a meeting in London over the weekend.
"For the market, the ACPC outcome should not be a problem, but GNI have a feeling that there will be still be a sell-off anyway," broker GNI said in a daily commentary.
The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) also said members' exports totalled 44.837 million bags for the year to June 1996 against a target of 45.841 million.
The 14-member ACPC had agreed in May to limit members' exports to 53.5 million 60-kg bags for the year to June 1997. But it did not discount the need for a revision if prices continue to slip.
In switches, Jan/March spread saw offers at $32.
